supplement.name: Family Studies
supplement.definition: Research that compares relatives to estimate how much a trait is influenced by shared genes and shared environment.

supplement.name: Adoption Studies
supplement.definition: Research comparing adopted children with their biological and adoptive relatives to separate genetic from environmental influences.

supplement.name: Adaptation
supplement.definition: An inherited or learned characteristic that increases an organism's chances of survival and reproduction.

supplement.name: Survival & Reproduction
supplement.definition: The evolutionary outcomes favored by natural selection: living long enough to reproduce and passing genes to the next generation.

supplement.name: Eugenics
supplement.definition: The discredited attempt to improve a population's genetic quality through selective breeding or reproduction policies.

supplement.name: Brain
supplement.definition: The organ of the central nervous system that integrates sensory information, coordinates behavior, and supports cognition.

supplement.name: Pituitary Gland
supplement.definition: The 'master gland' at the base of the brain that releases hormones controlling growth, reproduction, and other endocrine glands.

supplement.name: Adrenaline / Epinephrine
supplement.definition: A hormone and neurotransmitter released by the adrenal glands that increases arousal and supports the fight-or-flight response.

supplement.name: Leptin & Ghrelin
supplement.definition: Appetite-regulating hormones: leptin signals satiety, while ghrelin signals hunger.

supplement.name: Melatonin
supplement.definition: A hormone secreted by the pineal gland that helps regulate the sleep-wake cycle and circadian rhythm.

supplement.name: Oxytocin
supplement.definition: A hormone associated with bonding, trust, childbirth, and social affiliation.

supplement.name: Homeostasis
supplement.definition: The body's tendency to maintain a stable internal state around a set point.

supplement.name: Repolarization
supplement.definition: The phase of an action potential in which the neuron's membrane potential returns toward its resting negative charge.

supplement.name: Refractory Period
supplement.definition: A brief period after an action potential when a neuron cannot fire again or is harder to excite.

supplement.name: Pituitary Gland
supplement.definition: The 'master gland' at the base of the brain that releases hormones controlling growth, reproduction, and other endocrine glands.

supplement.name: Hippocampus
supplement.definition: A limbic-system structure important for forming new explicit memories and for spatial navigation.

supplement.name: Visual Cortex
supplement.definition: The occipital-lobe area that processes visual features such as edges, color, and motion.

supplement.name: Auditory Cortex
supplement.definition: The temporal-lobe area that processes sound and supports hearing.

supplement.name: Rewarding Center
supplement.definition: A brain circuit, including limbic and dopamine pathways, that produces reinforcement and pleasure.

supplement.name: Younger Brains Are More Malleable
supplement.definition: The developing brain shows greater neuroplasticity, making it more adaptable to experience and injury than the adult brain.

supplement.name: Long-Term Potentiation (LTP)
supplement.definition: A lasting increase in synaptic strength after repeated stimulation, considered a cellular basis of learning and memory.

supplement.name: Brain Stimulation
supplement.definition: Research or clinical techniques that apply electrical or magnetic stimulation to brain regions to study or alter function.

children.label: CAT / CT Scan
children.concept: Computerized axial tomography (CAT or CT) scan

supplement.name: Adaptive Theory
supplement.definition: The theory that sleep evolved because it provided survival advantages, such as conserving energy and avoiding danger.

supplement.name: Difference Threshold
supplement.definition: The smallest detectable difference between two stimuli, also called the just-noticeable difference.

supplement.name: Visual Cortex
supplement.definition: The occipital-lobe area that processes visual features such as edges, color, and motion.

supplement.name: Light Adaptation
supplement.definition: The process by which the eyes adjust to bright light, reducing sensitivity and shifting from rods to cones.

supplement.name: Dark Adaptation
supplement.definition: The process by which the eyes adjust to dim light, increasing sensitivity as rods take over.

supplement.name: External Ear
supplement.definition: The outer part of the ear, including the pinna and ear canal, that collects and directs sound waves.

supplement.name: Basilar Membrane
supplement.definition: The membrane inside the cochlea that vibrates in response to sound and supports hair cells that transduce pitch.

supplement.name: Volley Theory
supplement.definition: A pitch theory proposing that groups of auditory neurons fire in alternating volleys to encode frequencies higher than any single neuron can follow.

supplement.name: Divided Attention
supplement.definition: The attempt to process two or more streams of information at the same time, often with reduced performance on at least one task.

supplement.name: Context effect
supplement.definition: The influence of surrounding context or setting on perception, memory, or interpretation.

supplement.name: Apparent movement
supplement.definition: The illusion that a stationary object is moving, or that movement occurs between separated stimuli, as in the phi phenomenon.

supplement.name: Pictorial Depth Cues
supplement.definition: Monocular cues in a flat image—such as linear perspective, relative size, and overlap—that create an impression of depth.

supplement.name: Constancies
supplement.definition: Perceptual constancies are the tendency to perceive objects as stable in size, shape, brightness, or color despite changes in the retinal image.

supplement.name: Proximity
supplement.definition: A Gestalt grouping principle: stimuli near one another tend to be perceived as belonging together.

supplement.name: Similarity
supplement.definition: A Gestalt grouping principle: stimuli that look alike tend to be grouped together.

supplement.name: Figure-ground illusion
supplement.definition: A perceptual illusion in which the distinction between the main object (figure) and its background (ground) becomes ambiguous or reversible.

supplement.name: Assimilation
supplement.definition: Interpreting new experiences in terms of existing schemas or mental frameworks.

supplement.name: Accommodation
supplement.definition: Changing an existing schema or creating a new one to fit new information.

supplement.name: Hindsight Bias
supplement.definition: The tendency to believe, after learning an outcome, that one would have foreseen it; the 'I-knew-it-all-along' effect.

supplement.name: Priming
supplement.definition: The activation of a prior stimulus or memory that influences later perception, thinking, or behavior, often outside awareness.

supplement.name: Retrospective memory
supplement.definition: Memory for information or events from the past, such as facts, experiences, or prior actions.

supplement.name: Intermediate/phonemic encoding
supplement.definition: Encoding based on the sound of information, such as repeating or rehearsing words by how they sound.

supplement.name: Distributed Practice
supplement.definition: Spacing study or practice across multiple sessions over time, which usually improves long-term retention compared with massed practice.

supplement.name: Cerebellum
supplement.definition: A hindbrain structure important for balance, coordination, and motor learning.

supplement.name: Amygdala
supplement.definition: A limbic-system structure involved in emotion, especially fear learning and emotional salience.

supplement.name: Context-Dependent Memory
supplement.definition: Memory that is better recalled when the retrieval context matches the encoding context.

supplement.name: Metacognition
supplement.definition: Thinking about one's own thinking; monitoring and regulating cognitive processes.

supplement.name: Nonsense Syllables
supplement.definition: Meaningless consonant-vowel-consonant strings used by Ebbinghaus to study learning and forgetting without prior associations.

supplement.name: Retention
supplement.definition: The amount of learned material that can be recalled or recognized after a delay.

supplement.name: Savings Scores
supplement.definition: Ebbinghaus's measure of retention based on how much faster relearning is compared with original learning.

supplement.name: Encoding failure theory
supplement.definition: The explanation that forgetting occurs because information was never successfully encoded into long-term memory.

supplement.name: Repression
supplement.definition: A defense mechanism in which anxiety-provoking thoughts or memories are pushed out of conscious awareness.

supplement.name: Imagination inflation
supplement.definition: The finding that imagining an event can increase confidence that it actually occurred.

supplement.name: Giftedness
supplement.definition: Exceptional intellectual ability, often defined by high IQ or outstanding performance in a domain.

supplement.name: Hereditary Genius
supplement.definition: Galton's idea that eminence runs in families and is strongly influenced by heredity.

supplement.name: Alfred Binet
supplement.definition: French psychologist who developed an early intelligence test to identify children needing educational support.

supplement.name: Deviation IQ scores
supplement.definition: IQ scores based on how far a person's score deviates from the age-group average, expressed with a standard deviation.

supplement.name: Intellectual Disability
supplement.definition: A condition involving significantly below-average intellectual functioning and limitations in adaptive behavior; the modern term is intellectual disability.

supplement.name: Reaction range
supplement.definition: The idea that genotype sets a range of possible phenotypes, with environment determining where within that range a person develops.

supplement.name: Test norms
supplement.definition: Performance standards based on a representative sample, used to interpret test scores.

supplement.name: Criterion-related validity
supplement.definition: The degree to which test scores predict or correlate with a relevant external criterion.

3.1.label: Themes and Methods in Developmental Psychology

supplement.name: Continuity vs Discontinuity
supplement.definition: The developmental issue of whether development is gradual and continuous or occurs in distinct stages.

supplement.name: Stability vs Change
supplement.definition: The developmental issue of whether traits remain stable across the lifespan or change with age and experience.

supplement.name: Naturalistic Observation
supplement.definition: Observing behavior in naturally occurring settings without manipulating variables.

supplement.name: Meta-Analysis
supplement.definition: A statistical technique that combines results from many studies to estimate an overall effect.

supplement.name: Experimenter Bias
supplement.definition: Researcher expectations influencing the results or the behavior of participants.

supplement.name: Informed Consent
supplement.definition: Participants receive enough information to decide voluntarily whether to take part in research.

supplement.name: Confidentiality
supplement.definition: Researchers protect participants' identity and data from unauthorized disclosure.

supplement.name: Gross-to-Fine Direction
supplement.definition: Motor development proceeds from large, gross movements to precise, fine movements.

supplement.name: Head-to-Foot Direction
supplement.definition: Motor development proceeds from the head and upper body toward the lower body.

supplement.name: Hormonal Changes
supplement.definition: Age-related shifts in hormone levels that affect physical, reproductive, and emotional development.

supplement.name: Hearing & Vision Decline
supplement.definition: Normal aging changes that reduce sensory acuity, especially high-frequency hearing and near vision.

supplement.name: Dementia
supplement.definition: A progressive cognitive decline affecting memory, reasoning, language, and daily functioning.

supplement.name: Gender Stereotypes
supplement.definition: Widely held beliefs about the traits and behaviors considered appropriate for men and women.

supplement.name: Sexual Orientation
supplement.definition: A person's enduring pattern of emotional, romantic, or sexual attraction.

supplement.name: Schema Theory
supplement.definition: The idea that people organize knowledge into mental frameworks (schemas) that guide interpretation and memory.

supplement.name: Language & Thought
supplement.definition: The relationship between language and cognition, including claims that language shapes thought.

supplement.name: Fluid vs Crystallized Intelligence
supplement.definition: Fluid intelligence is reasoning and solving new problems; crystallized intelligence is accumulated knowledge and skills.

supplement.name: Dementia
supplement.definition: A progressive cognitive decline affecting memory, reasoning, language, and daily functioning.

supplement.name: Nonverbal gesture
supplement.definition: Communication through body movements, facial expressions, posture, and gestures rather than words.

supplement.name: Cooing
supplement.definition: Early infant vowel-like sounds produced before canonical babbling.

supplement.name: Babbling
supplement.definition: Repetitive consonant-vowel sounds in infancy that precede first words.

supplement.name: Neglectful Parenting
supplement.definition: A parenting style low in warmth and low in control, in which caregivers are relatively uninvolved.

supplement.name: Disorganized Attachment
supplement.definition: Inconsistent or contradictory attachment behavior, often associated with frightening or unpredictable caregiving.

supplement.name: Pretend Play
supplement.definition: Symbolic play in which children act out roles, scenarios, or imaginary situations.

supplement.name: Parallel Play
supplement.definition: Children play side by side with similar toys but with little direct interaction.

supplement.name: Adolescent Egocentrism
supplement.definition: Heightened self-consciousness and difficulty distinguishing one's own perspective from others'.

supplement.name: Identity Statuses (Marcia)
supplement.definition: Four identity statuses—diffusion, foreclosure, moratorium, and achievement—based on exploration and commitment.

supplement.name: Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs)
supplement.definition: Potentially traumatic childhood events associated with later psychological and physical health risk.

supplement.name: Positive Reinforcement
supplement.definition: Increasing a behavior by adding a desirable consequence after it occurs.

supplement.name: Negative Reinforcement
supplement.definition: Increasing a behavior by removing or avoiding an unpleasant consequence.

supplement.name: Positive Punishment
supplement.definition: Decreasing a behavior by adding an unpleasant consequence.

supplement.name: Negative Punishment
supplement.definition: Decreasing a behavior by removing a desirable consequence.

supplement.name: Illusory correlation
supplement.definition: Perceiving a relationship between variables that does not exist or is weaker than believed.

supplement.name: Learned Helplessness
supplement.definition: Passivity and reduced effort after repeated exposure to uncontrollable failure.

3.9.label: Social, Cognitive, and Neurological Factors in Learning

supplement.name: Self-Efficacy
supplement.definition: Belief in one's ability to succeed at a specific task or in a particular situation.

supplement.name: Attributions
supplement.definition: Explanations people construct for the causes of events and behavior.

supplement.name: Optimistic Explanatory Style
supplement.definition: Explaining negative events with external, temporary, and specific causes.

supplement.name: Pessimistic Explanatory Style
supplement.definition: Explaining negative events with internal, stable, and global causes.

supplement.name: Culture and Attributional Tendencies
supplement.definition: Cultural differences in attribution, such as individualistic cultures favoring dispositional explanations.

supplement.name: Stereotypes, Prejudice & Discrimination
supplement.definition: Stereotypes are beliefs, prejudice is negative attitude, and discrimination is unequal behavior toward a group.

supplement.name: Belief Perseverance
supplement.definition: Clinging to a belief even after the evidence supporting it has been discredited.

supplement.name: Confirmation Bias
supplement.definition: Seeking or interpreting information in ways that support existing beliefs.

supplement.name: Informational Social Influence
supplement.definition: Conformity because one believes others have accurate information.

supplement.name: Normative Social Influence
supplement.definition: Conformity to gain social approval or avoid rejection.

supplement.name: Compliance
supplement.definition: Changing behavior in response to a direct request, without necessarily changing private beliefs.

supplement.name: Social inhibition
supplement.definition: Reduced performance or expressiveness when others are present.

supplement.name: Milgram's Experiment
supplement.definition: An obedience study in which participants followed authority instructions to administer apparently painful shocks.

supplement.name: Prisoner's Dilemma
supplement.definition: A social trap in which individual self-interest produces a worse joint outcome.

supplement.name: Multiculturalism
supplement.definition: Recognizing and maintaining multiple cultural identities within a society or person.

4.4.label: Psychodynamic and Humanistic Theories of Personality

supplement.name: Conscious
supplement.definition: The level of awareness that includes current thoughts, perceptions, and feelings.

supplement.name: Preconscious
supplement.definition: Information outside current awareness that can be brought into consciousness easily.

supplement.name: Psychosexual Stages
supplement.definition: Freud's oral, anal, phallic, latency, and genital stages of personality development.

supplement.name: Incongruence
supplement.definition: A mismatch between one's real self and ideal self, which Rogers saw as a source of distress.

supplement.name: Unconditional Positive Regard
supplement.definition: Acceptance and valuing of a person without conditions or contingencies.

4.5.label: Social-Cognitive and Trait Theories of Personality

supplement.name: Observational Learning
supplement.definition: Learning by watching the behavior and consequences of models.

supplement.name: Factor Analysis
supplement.definition: A statistical method for identifying clusters of items or traits that correlate.

supplement.name: Openness
supplement.definition: Big Five trait reflecting imagination, curiosity, and openness to new experience.

supplement.name: Conscientiousness
supplement.definition: Big Five trait reflecting organization, responsibility, and self-discipline.

supplement.name: Extraversion
supplement.definition: Big Five trait reflecting sociability, assertiveness, and positive emotionality.

supplement.name: Agreeableness
supplement.definition: Big Five trait reflecting cooperation, trust, and concern for others.

supplement.name: Neuroticism
supplement.definition: Big Five trait reflecting emotional instability and proneness to negative affect.

supplement.name: Person-Situation Controversy
supplement.definition: The debate over whether personality traits or situational factors better predict behavior.

supplement.name: Approach-Approach
supplement.definition: A conflict between two desirable options.

supplement.name: Avoidance-Avoidance
supplement.definition: A conflict between two undesirable options.

supplement.name: Avoidance-Approach
supplement.definition: A conflict involving a single option with both desirable and undesirable features.

supplement.name: Thrill and Adventure Seeking (TAS)
supplement.definition: Sensation-seeking facet involving attraction to risky, exciting activities.

supplement.name: Experience Seeking (ES)
supplement.definition: Sensation-seeking facet involving novelty and unconventional experiences.

supplement.name: Disinhibition (DS)
supplement.definition: Sensation-seeking facet involving reduced restraint and enjoyment of losing inhibitions.

supplement.name: Boredom Susceptibility (BS)
supplement.definition: Sensation-seeking facet involving intolerance of repetitive or boring situations.

supplement.name: Incentive theories
supplement.definition: Theories that motivation is driven by external rewards, punishments, and incentives.

supplement.name: Amygdala
supplement.definition: A limbic-system structure involved in emotion, especially fear learning and emotional salience.

supplement.name: Sympathetic nervous system
supplement.definition: The branch of the autonomic nervous system that prepares the body for fight-or-flight.

supplement.name: Schachter Two-Factor Theory
supplement.definition: Emotion results from physiological arousal plus a cognitive label for that arousal.

supplement.name: Lazarus's Appraisal Theory
supplement.definition: Emotion depends on cognitive appraisal of an event's meaning and significance.

supplement.name: Positive and Negative Emotions
supplement.definition: Positive emotions tend to broaden thinking and build resources; negative emotions tend to narrow attention and support specific responses.

supplement.name: Universal/Evolutionary Theories of Emotion
supplement.definition: The view that certain basic emotions are innate and universally recognizable because they had adaptive value.

supplement.name: Eustress
supplement.definition: Positive or motivating stress that can improve performance and growth.

supplement.name: Distress
supplement.definition: Negative stress that feels overwhelming and can impair health and performance.

supplement.name: Alarm Reaction
supplement.definition: The first stage of the general adaptation syndrome, when the body mobilizes resources to meet a stressor.

supplement.name: Deviance
supplement.definition: Behavior that violates social norms or expectations and is one criterion of abnormality.

supplement.name: Personal Distress
supplement.definition: Subjective suffering or impairment that is one criterion of abnormal behavior.

supplement.name: Maladaptive Behavior
supplement.definition: Behavior that interferes with everyday functioning and well-being.

children.label: Diagnosis
children.concept: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM)

supplement.name: Evolutionary Perspective
supplement.definition: Explaining behavior through the adaptive value of traits selected over evolutionary history.

supplement.name: Sociocultural Perspective
supplement.definition: Explaining behavior through social and cultural context, norms, and group membership.

supplement.name: Biological Perspective
supplement.definition: Explaining behavior through genetics, brain structure, neurotransmitters, and physiology.

supplement.name: Categories of Disorders
supplement.definition: DSM categories group disorders by shared symptoms, course, and clinical features.

5.4.label: Selection of Categories of Psychological Disorders

supplement.name: Genetic Vulnerability
supplement.definition: Inherited predisposition that increases risk for a disorder.

supplement.name: Neurochemical Factors
supplement.definition: Differences in neurotransmitter activity or brain chemistry associated with a disorder.

supplement.name: Neurodevelopmental Hypothesis
supplement.definition: The idea that schizophrenia results in part from disrupted brain development early in life.

supplement.name: Expressed Emotion
supplement.definition: Family criticism, hostility, or emotional overinvolvement associated with relapse risk.

supplement.name: Genetic Factors
supplement.definition: Inherited influences that contribute to risk for a disorder.

supplement.name: Neurochemical Factors
supplement.definition: Differences in neurotransmitter activity or brain chemistry associated with a disorder.

supplement.name: Cognitive Factors
supplement.definition: Maladaptive beliefs, appraisals, and thinking patterns that contribute to a disorder.

supplement.name: Biological Factors
supplement.definition: Genetic, neurological, or physiological influences on a disorder.

supplement.name: Conditioning & Learning
supplement.definition: Classical and operant learning processes that can create or maintain fear and avoidance.

supplement.name: Cognitive Factors
supplement.definition: Maladaptive beliefs, appraisals, and thinking patterns that contribute to a disorder.

supplement.name: Stress
supplement.definition: Psychological and physiological strain produced by demanding or threatening events.

supplement.name: Obsessions
supplement.definition: Intrusive, unwanted thoughts, images, or urges that cause distress.

supplement.name: Compulsions
supplement.definition: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed to reduce distress or prevent a feared outcome.

supplement.name: Dissociative Fugue
supplement.definition: Sudden travel away from home with confusion about identity, often following stress or trauma.

supplement.name: Etiology
supplement.definition: The causes and maintaining factors that explain how a disorder develops.

supplement.name: Histrionic Personality Disorder
supplement.definition: A personality disorder marked by attention-seeking, dramatic behavior, and shallow emotions.
